fields.title: Changes reach production through the pipeline

sections.Purpose: The pipeline is the only route into production. A trivial change takes it and so does an urgent one. The one exception, for an outage, is recorded at the time and reconciled afterwards.
sections.Scope:
Production and any environment where a change affects customers or contains real data. Applies equally to application deployments, infrastructure changes, configuration changes and database changes.

_Boundary: this policy governs the route a change takes into production and the approval behind it. [pol-TRUS](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b0333383184268b860732fbaaad3e8631faa0ba1/examples/engineering/policies/security/trus-trusted-components.md#clauses) owns what an artefact is made of, where it is kept and whether its origin can be proved. A deployment that does not go as expected is an operational incident: [pol-INCR](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b0333383184268b860732fbaaad3e8631faa0ba1/examples/engineering/policies/operations/incr-incident-response.md#clauses).LEARN reviews it._
sections.Exceptions: An emergency change to restore service may bypass the normal path where the pipeline is itself unavailable, or where the delay would extend an outage. It is recorded as a deviation under [pol-DEVI](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b0333383184268b860732fbaaad3e8631faa0ba1/examples/engineering/policies/governance/devi-deviations.md) at the time, and the change is reconciled back into version control before the incident is closed. Otherwise the fix becomes the next outage.
